sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:57

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:57:1
items.html:
And this vessel fell in the place of Daat of Beria, being related to it as its like: The cause of the breaking has already been well explained above in the Inner Light (page 463, the passage beginning “The dross”), study it there well. Therefore they were separated from holiness, as written there.
As for the matter of their fall into the three worlds BYA of which the ARI speaks, although these three worlds did not yet exist at all, still their record was discernible, for they are the phase of the three Sefirot Bina, ZA and Malchut of NHY of the Sium, which came out outside the Atzilut of AK at the time of the second restriction, as is written at length above (page 399, in the Inner Light, the passage beginning “The second restriction”). And since each one of these kings was included of ten Sefirot, which are Rosh, Toch, Sof [RTS], their Rosh [head] fell into Beria, their Toch fell into Yetzira, and their Sof fell into Assiya. And what the ARI writes, that the vessel of Daat fell into the Daat of Beria, refers to the phase of its Rosh, which is KHBD of Daat, whereas its HGT fell into Yetzira and its NHYM fell into Assiya. In this way you will understand the matter of the fall of all seven kings.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:57:2
items.html: Being related to it as its like: For in each world of the three worlds BYA there are ten Sefirot, and therefore the vessel of the king Daat fell into the Daat of Beria, that is, into the very phase that stands opposite it.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:57:3
items.html: The light of Daat descended as well, except that it remained in Atzilut, etc., in order to illuminate from afar into its vessel that stands in Beria: Know that this light of which the ARI speaks is the record that remained from the light of Daat after its departure from the vessel. For every light leaves a record behind it after its departure, and by this it illuminates the vessel so that it will not be nullified and will not die, as above in the words of the ARI (Part 4, Chapter 2, item 2 and item 8). And the ARI informs us that the record of Daat did not remain in the vessel itself, as is its way in the previous Partzufim, but rather remained in Atzilut. And this is what he says: “For the breaking was in the vessels and not in the lights … and it is in the phase of Tagin [crowns] upon the letters.” For the light of the record that cannot, for some reason, clothe inside the vessel, and illuminates the vessel from afar, is called Tagin, as above in the words of the ARI (Part 4, Chapter 3, item 11), see there.
